title: Java Constructors
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose of a constructor during object creation.
Declare a constructor with the same name as its class.
Initialize object fields using constructor parameters.
Distinguish a no-argument constructor from a parameterized constructor.
Explain when Java supplies a default constructor and when it does not.

understand.concept: A constructor is a special class member used to initialize a new object. It has the same name as its class and has no return type. A class can declare multiple constructors with different parameter lists. If no constructor is declared, Java provides a default no-argument constructor.
understand.whyItMatters: Constructors help ensure objects begin in a valid, predictable state. Requiring essential values at creation time can prevent partially initialized objects.
understand.analogy: Think of a well-designed object as a small service with a clear responsibility: it keeps the information it owns and exposes only the operations other code needs.
understand.analogyLimit: This analogy is only a design aid; Java access, inheritance and dispatch follow the language's exact rules.

explain.narrative:
## Constructor syntax

A constructor has the class name and no return type, not even void. It runs when an object is created with new.

## No-argument and parameterized constructors

A no-argument constructor accepts no parameters. A parameterized constructor receives values and can use them to initialize fields. Constructors can be overloaded.

## Default constructor rule

If a class declares no constructor, the compiler provides a default no-argument constructor. Once any constructor is declared, Java does not automatically add that default constructor.

## Common mistakes

- Writing a return type before a constructor name.
- Giving the constructor a different name from the class.
- Assuming a default constructor remains available after declaring another constructor.

examples.title: No-argument constructor
examples.code:
class Device { Device() { System.out.println("Created"); } }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { new Device(); } }
examples.explanation: The constructor runs as the Device object is created.

examples.title: Initialize fields with parameters
examples.code:
class Person { String name; Person(String value) { name = value; } }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Person p = new Person("Asha"); System.out.println(p.name); } }
examples.explanation: The constructor receives a value and stores it in the new object.

examples.title: Overload constructors
examples.code:
class Point { int x; int y; Point() { x = 0; y = 0; } Point(int a, int b) { x = a; y = b; } }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Point p = new Point(3, 4); System.out.println(p.x + p.y); } }
examples.explanation: Different parameter lists allow more than one constructor.

examples.title: Use this to distinguish a field
examples.code:
class Account { int balance; Account(int balance) { this.balance = balance; } }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { System.out.println(new Account(50).balance); } }
examples.explanation: this.balance identifies the field while balance is the parameter.

examples.title: Constructor runs for every new instance
examples.code:
class Ticket { static int issued = 0; Ticket() { issued++; } }
public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { new Ticket(); new Ticket(); new Ticket(); System.out.println(Ticket.issued); } }
examples.explanation: Each object creation invokes its constructor once.

questions.prompt: What is a constructor used for?
options: Returning a value from a method
questions.explanation: Constructors establish an object's initial state.

questions.prompt: Does a constructor have a return type?
What must a constructor's name match?
questions.explanation: The constructor name is exactly the class name.

questions.prompt: When does Java provide a default no-argument constructor?
options: Only when a field is static
questions.explanation: The compiler supplies one only if the class declares no constructor.

questions.prompt: What happens after a class declares a parameterized constructor but no no-argument constructor?
questions.answer: A no-argument constructor is not supplied automatically
options: A no-argument constructor is not supplied automatically
questions.explanation: Declaring any constructor suppresses the implicit default constructor.
